tools.description: Beam does not upload or submit feedback. This tool creates and returns a pasteable feedback report for one explicit workspace. Non-confidential output may contain project context and caller payloads, so review it before posting. Set confidential for non-public workspaces; confidential results retain caller-authored narrative except for HOME-path redaction and do not scan it for other secrets; never post them publicly. A local evidence bundle is optional.

bundle.description: Optional evidence bundle mode. Defaults to none.

confidential.description: Set true for a non-public workspace. Forces HOME-path redaction; omits automatically collected project debug context, caller-supplied request, response, evidence, and the echoed workspace descriptor; retains other caller-authored narrative without scanning it for arbitrary secrets; and marks the report as confidential. Defaults to false.

evidence.description: Optional evidence entries to include in a bundle.

items.description: Optional inline or file evidence to copy into a feedback bundle.

content.description: Inline JSON or text evidence to write into the bundle.

name.description: Simple evidence filename, without path separators.

path.description: Path to a local evidence file under the known root or selected Beam session directory.

include_collected.description: When true, include collected Beam debug context inline in the MCP result. In confidential mode, include only the restricted runtime identity. Defaults to false.

redact.description: Whether to redact the user's home directory from the rendered report. Defaults to true.

reproduction.description: Concrete steps or commands needed to reproduce the behavior.

request.description: Optional request payload relevant to the report.

response.description: Optional response payload relevant to the report.

summary.description: What went wrong or what feedback should be reviewed.

tags.description: Optional short labels for routing the report.

tools.name: beam_feedback_report

tools.description: Speculatively run one Lean command or tactic block at a file position. The text is not persisted as source and no follow-up state is kept. To keep a result, first edit and save the Lean file yourself, then call lean_sync. Tactic probes reject new local `let rec` definitions, even valid ones; save the enclosing declaration and sync instead. Probes are not an OS sandbox: Lean code may perform IO.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to a regular .lean source inside the workspace root.

text.description: One Lean command or tactic block to run at the selected position. Top-level command sequences are not accepted by one runAt call.

version.description: Document version returned by a successful update or sync operation for this file.

tools.description: Inspect agent-actionable Lean todo items in a file, or in an optional range. Sorry, hole, and incomplete-proof items carry the goal that run_at sees at their run_at_position; run_at_position is omitted when no source position selects that goal. Code actions use one command snapshot selected by the range end; prefer a point inside the relevant syntax or a range within one command. An empty code-action result does not establish whole-range or whole-file completeness.
